newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp seeks Loewen Group.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp seeks Loewen Group.

text.p: Service Corp International said Monday it proposed acquiring Loewen Group Inc in a stock-for-stock exchange that values Lowen at US$43 per share.
Service Corp said the offer was made in a letter to Loewen chief executive Raymond L. Loewen, which pointed out the proposal is based on public information.
"After due diligence review, we may be in a position to increase the consideration that your stockholders would receive," it continued.
Service Corp said the proposed "combination is planned as a pooling of interests and is anticipated to be accretive to earnings."
Chief executive Robert L. Waltrip said "This proposal will create a combined company with unparalleled resources."
If completed, the company said, the transaction would resuilt in an entity comprised of about 3,750 funeral homes and 600 cemeteries worldwide.
In the letter, Service Corp President L. William Heiligbrodt said he had tried to reach Loewen several times since September 11, but "my calls have not been returned."
"In view of that, and in view of the importance of this matter, I am sending this letter."

He said "We believe that this transaction can be structured in a manner that is tax-free to both companies and (except for a relatively nominal amount in the case of U.S. stockholders) to the U.S. and Canadian stockholders of Loewen Group."

Recognizing "that our businesses overlap in various locations," the letter said Service Corp is "convinced that competition issues can be cured by selected divestitures without impairment of the values that a combination would achieve for the stockholders of our two companies.

"I would very much like to discuss any and all aspects of our proposal directly with you and your board of directors," Heiligbrodt continued, adding "Our proposal is conditioned upon approval of our board and upon negotiation of mutually satisfactory agreements providing for a combination on a pooling basis." -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
